BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION

 IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF EL                                 )
 PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY FOR REVISION OF                                  )
 ITS RETAIL ELECTRIC RATES,                                             ) Docket No. 25-00082-UT
 EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY,                                              )
 Applicant.                                                             )

                      ORDER SHORTENING DEADLINE FOR RESPONSES

         THIS MATTER comes before the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission

(“Commission”) upon El Paso Electric Company’s (“EPE”) Unopposed And Verified Motion For

Variance Regarding Rate Case Filing Deadline (“Motion”). With this order the Commission

shortens the deadline for responses to EPE’s Motion, and clarifies that the Motion shall be assessed

as a motion for extension of time, in accordance with Rule 1.2.2.8(K) NMAC.

                                             DISCUSSION

         1.       On February 6, 2026, EPE filed its Motion for “an order granting EPE a variance

from the requirement that it file its rate case package no later than 150 days after the last day of

the Base Period.” 1 EPE sought the positions of parties to its most recent rate case, Case No. 20-

00104-UT, and no opposition was expressed by those parties. 2

         2.       EPE seeks a four-week extension of the deadline for its rate case filing to be

tendered, which would allow EPE to file its rate case on or before March 27, 2026, with a base

period ending on September 30, 2025. 3

         3.       EPE styled its request as a motion for a variance, but in this specific instance EPE’s

request also qualifies as a request for an extension of time under Rule 1.2.2.8(K) NMAC.



1 Motion (February 6, 2026) at 1.


2 Id. ¶ 18.


3 Id. ¶¶ 5-6, and ¶ 13.
         4.       Administrative efficiency will be promoted by considering EPE’s Motion as a

motion for extension of time, 4 as the chairman of the Commission or any other Commissioner may

issue a procedural order that addresses EPE’s motion for an extension of time. 5

        5.       Rule 1.2.2.8(K) NMAC establishes that the time by which any person is required

to act under any rule may be extended by the commission or presiding officer for good cause.

        IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED:

        A.       EPE’s Motion shall be addressed by the Commission as a motion for extension of

time.

        B.       Responses to EPE’s Motion may be filed by February 17, 2026.

        C.       This Order is effective when signed.

        D.       In computing time in accordance with statute, regulation, or Commission order, the

computation shall begin on the date that this Order is filed with the Chief Clerk of the

Commission’s Records Management Bureau or the Chief Clerk’s designee.

        SIGNED under the Seal of the Commission at Santa Fe, New Mexico, this 12th day of

February, 2026.

                            NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION


                            /s/ Gabriel Aguilera, electronically signed
                             GABRIEL AGUILERA, COMMISSIONER




4 See Rule 1.2.2.11(G) NMAC: All pleadings shall be liberally construed and errors or defects therein which do

not mislead or affect the substantial rights of staff and the parties involved shall be disregarded. See also Rule
1.2.2.8(E) NMAC: These rules, and any rules incorporated by reference, shall be so construed as to secure just
and speedy determination of the issues.
5 Rule 1.2.2.30 (B) NMAC.
